Geodynamics • Earthquake Physics • Multiscale Modeling

Physics-based modeling of plate tectonics, earthquake rupture, and planetary evolution.

I am a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Laboratoire de Géologie de l'École Normale Supérieure - PSL. My research focuses on developing a unified, physics-based understanding of lithospheric dynamics across timescales—from long-term tectonic evolution to short-term earthquake rupture—using advanced 2D and 3D numerical models constrained by laboratory experiments and geological–geophysical observations.

At A Glance

Research Overview

Research I

Mid-Ocean Ridge Dynamics

Research on how magma supply, faulting, and lithospheric deformation interact to shape the tectonic evolution of mid-ocean ridges.

Research II

Subudction Zone Evolution

Research on how fluids and melts weaken tectonic plates, promote lithospheric thinning, and drive plate destruction.

Research III

Transform Fault Seismicity

Integrating lab-derived friction laws into earthquake cycle simulations to understand rupture dynamics.
